name: common-qa-mcp

tools.name: project_info
tools.description: Validate the configured connection and return provider, org/project and entity counts.

tools.name: qa_connect
tools.description:
Point this MCP at your QA product so it can work with EXISTING test cases -- list them, read their steps, modify them, and run them. Ask the user for their app URL and a token; do not guess either. The token is a product session JWT (then `projectId` is required, because the token alone carries no project context) or an MCP API key (then pass auth:"key" and projectId is optional -- a key is already project-scoped).

The connection is VALIDATED before it is accepted (it fetches the project), so a wrong URL, token or project fails here with the reason rather than surfacing later as a confusing error, and a failed attempt leaves any working connection untouched. It is kept in memory for as long as the agent runs and is never written to disk or logged.

NOT needed to record a new test case: recording, the live editor and drafts work offline with nothing configured.

url.description: MCP endpoint to hop to — the product agent /mcp, used for recording and save-with-editor. OPTIONAL for a DIRECT (backend-REST) connection: pass `baseUrl` instead. Required when connecting through a remote product MCP. Must start with http:// or https://.

token.description: Bearer token: a product session JWT, or an MCP API key.

projectId.description: Project id. REQUIRED with a JWT; optional with an API key.

auth.description: Token kind. Omit to AUTO-DETECT from the token (JWT-shaped → "jwt"). "jwt" sends Authorization + x-project-id; "key" sends Authorization only.

product.description: Which product to route this connection to (the product selector; defaults to the primary product). For a remote product, also pass its agent MCP `/mcp` endpoint as `url`.

baseUrl.description: The product BACKEND REST base (QA_BASE_URL) for DIRECT data ops (list/read/save/run). Provide this for a direct connection; `url` is only needed for recording / save-with-editor.

tools.name: qa_switch_project
tools.description: Switch to a different project on the SAME connection — reuses the current URL + token, so you do NOT re-enter them. Pass the project id; if the user names a project, resolve the name to an id first (SimplifyQA: sqa_query collection "projects" with member:true; Walnut: list_projects). Validated before it is adopted, so a bad id leaves the current project in place.

projectId.description: The project id to switch to. Find it by name with sqa_query collection "projects" (SimplifyQA) or list_projects (Walnut).

tools.name: qa_connection_status
tools.description: Report whether this MCP is connected to a QA product, which URL and project, how the credentials arrived (startup config vs qa_connect), and whether a token is present. Also reports whether the LOCAL desktop agent (/mcp, default :4040) is reachable — the process that actually runs LOCAL executions on this machine. The token value itself is never returned.

tools.name: qa_disconnect
tools.description: Forget the runtime URL and token and fall back to whatever the agent started with (usually nothing). Use it before connecting to a different app or project, or to stop this MCP reaching a backend at all. Offline authoring is unaffected.

tools.name: actions_catalog
tools.description: Static per-platform action-type vocabulary (web/android/ios/api/database/mainframe), used for offline draft validation. No network call. NOTE mainframe is deliberately EMPTY (no source list exists), and validate.ts skips validation entirely for an empty catalog — so a clean mainframe draft means "not checked", not "checked and fine".

platform.description: desktop: there is no offline list; on SimplifyQA the live catalog includes the DESKTOP actions (dsk-*: Launch Application, Click, Type Text, Switch to Window by Name, …).

tools.name: tc_draft_from_tc
tools.description:
Fetch a REAL test case from the connected product and hydrate it into a draft, carrying the original tcId. Because the draft carries the id, a later `tc_save({ draftId })` UPDATES that SAME test case (preserving id, run history, parameters, testdata bindings, and suite membership) instead of creating a sibling.

THIS is the tool for "tag/retag this EXISTING test case with a user story or module" — `journal_modify`'s `set_meta` does NOT support that on SimplifyQA (journal-only ops there), so this draft round-trip is the only path:
  1. tc_draft_from_tc({ tcId })
  2. tc_draft_update({ draftId, ops: [{ op: "set_meta", patch: { storyRef?, folderOrModule?, title?, priority?, ... } }] }) — resolve a story/module NAME to an id via story_list / list_modules FIRST; never guess one.
  3. tc_save({ draftId })
Same three steps also apply to applying a `story_sync_testcases` drift report (pass the filtered `proposedOps` at step 2 instead of a set_meta patch). Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

tcId.description: The existing test-case id to load as a draft.

tools.name: tc_draft_from_journal
tools.description: Load the steps from a recording session (the journal on the connected agent) into a new AUTOMATION draft. Use this to save a recording that finished — including one from an earlier session. Then review with tc_draft_get and persist with tc_save. If the recording targeted an existing TC, pass its id via `tcId` so the draft inherits title/module/project and tc_save UPDATES that TC instead of creating a new one. Requires a live connection (qa_connect) with an agent that owns the recording journal.

sessionId.description: The recording session id — the same id used when the recording started.

tcId.description: Optional: an existing TC id to inherit title/module/project from (and to UPDATE on save).

title.description: Optional draft title (overrides tcId meta). Defaults to "Recording <sessionId>" when no tcId is passed.

tools.name: tc_draft_create
tools.description:
MANUAL-ONLY authoring. Call this when the user asked for a MANUAL test case: they said "manual", "draft only", "plain prose", "no automation", or asked to cover a user story's acceptance criteria as manual cases. For those, this IS the right tool — call it.

Do NOT use for automated tests. "create a test case", "record this flow", "add a test for X" (with no "manual" qualifier) mean AUTOMATED — route to the `web` / `mainframe` sub-agent to RECORD with real locators instead.

Create a new in-memory test-case draft from steps you author yourself. Nothing is persisted -- no disk, no backend, no network. Use tc_draft_open to hand it to the test-case editor for viewing.

DO NOT USE THIS FOR A REAL WEB APPLICATION. Steps written here have no locators, so the test case cannot execute -- it only reads plausibly. Whenever there is an app you can reach (the user gives a URL, names an environment, or asks for a test of a real flow), call the `web` sub-agent instead: that captures real locators, real element names and real parameters, and is the DEFAULT way to create a web test case. You do not need the user to say "record" -- if a test case for a real app is wanted, recording is how it is made.

Legitimate uses: a MANUAL test case the user explicitly asked for (no automation), API/database steps that need no element binding, restructuring or drafting steps the user supplied verbatim, or sketching a plan when no app is reachable -- and say plainly that the result is not executable until recorded.

PARAMETERISE EVERY DYNAMIC VALUE — this is mandatory for manual test cases whenever the step names a URL, credential, product name, form value, expected string, or anything the tester will type / compare. Instead of hard-coding "Enter admin in the Username field", write "Enter ${username} in the Username field" and pass `data: { username: "admin" }` at the TC level. Every `${name}` token becomes a Local parameter in the product and the value from `data` populates the test case's default test-data row (ITR-1) automatically. Steps with no `${...}` tokens create no parameters — that is only correct for pure checklist verifications ("verify heading is visible"). If a step references a real value, tokenise it.

storyRef.description: Link this test case to a USER STORY — its id or business key (US_123, from story_list / story_get). Used when drafting MANUAL test cases for a story so they save linked to it.

folderOrModule.description: SimplifyQA-only: id of the MODULE / folder to file this test case under on save (from list_modules). ASK the user which module before drafting; SimplifyQA files test cases in a module tree. Walnut ignores this.

unique.description: true makes this the object's DEFAULT locator (the one the UI marks as default and the executor uses first); only one default exists — it is cleared on the others. object_update also has `defaultLocator` (by name).

data.description: Default values for the `${name}` tokens in step descriptions — one entry per token. Populates the auto-created default test-data row (ITR-1) on save. Example: `{ username: "admin", password: "admin123", url: "https://saucedemo.com" }`.

tools.name: tc_draft_update
tools.description:
Apply one or more ops (set_meta | add_step | update_step | remove_step | move_step | duplicate_step) to a draft. Steps renumber contiguously from 1 after every op.

To COPY a step ("add the same step 2 at the end") use duplicate_step { n, at? } — never rebuild it with add_step: duplicate_step clones the WHOLE step (parameters and their values, object, flags, browser, API request, settings) so nothing is lost. For an IF / loop / function block pass `through` too (the last step of the block).

update_steps { where, patch } applies ONE patch to EVERY step matching `where` (numbers, from/to, stepType, actionType, object, descriptionContains, parameter) — use it for "skip every step that uses X"; an empty `where` is refused unless all:true. To change WHICH parameter a step uses, put `swapParams: [{ from, to, value? }]` in the step patch (it replaces the parameter in the SAME slot; `recordedParam` only adds). To edit a project parameter itself (Local <-> Runtime, default value) use parameter_update.
To change an API step IN PLACE (add an assertion, change the URL / a header / the body) use update_step with `patch.api`: it is MERGED into the saved request, so only what you pass changes. `api.addAssertions: [{ path, condition, expectedValue }]` appends assertions (e.g. path "statusCode", "$.body.id", "$.headers.X"); `api.assertions` replaces the whole list. NEVER remove_step + add_step to edit a step — that deletes it and creates a different one.

STEP TYPE — for add_step / update_step on a MANUAL test case (tc.category === "manual", or every existing step arrived with stepType "manual"), pass `stepType: "manual"`. For an AUTOMATED test case pick the execution technology ("web", "api", "android", …). Getting this wrong routes the row to the wrong UI card and it renders blank in the desktop viewer.

CALLING A SAVED FUNCTION — a function step is `{ stepType: "function", actionType: "function", description, functionCall: { testCaseId: "FN-12" } }` (the numeric id also works). Its matching `function_end` row is generated automatically and the function's NEWEST version is pinned at save, so "use these functions and create a new tc" is just one add_step per function in run order, then tc_save. Do NOT pass a real action name (a function call has no action) and do NOT add `function_end` yourself.

unique.description: true makes this the object's DEFAULT locator (the one the UI marks as default and the executor uses first); only one default exists — it is cleared on the others. object_update also has `defaultLocator` (by name).

true makes this the object's DEFAULT locator (the one the UI marks as default and the executor uses first); only one default exists — it is cleared on the others. object_update also has `defaultLocator` (by name).

from.description: Parameter the step uses now (name, or numeric id).

to.description: Parameter to use instead (name; created when missing).

value.description: The new parameter's test-data value for this step.

n.description: Step number of an EXISTING API step.

path.description: Response path: statusCode | responseTime | responseSize | $.body.<path> (or response.<path>) | $.headers.<Name>.

condition.description: EQUALS | NOT_EQUALS | CONTAINS | DOES_NOT_CONTAIN | NOT_EMPTY | EQUAL_TO_EMPTY | EQUAL_TO_NULL | NOT_EQUAL_TO_NULL | GREATER_THAN | LESSER_THAN | GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO | LESSER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO (LESS_THAN is accepted and folded to LESSER_THAN).

key.description: Optional editor key (header name for $.headers.<Name>; inferred otherwise).

assertions.description: Assertions to APPEND to that step. The request, object, action, parameters and existing assertions are left untouched.

numbers.description: Step numbers to delete, in any order — resolved against the current steps, so a range (5..10) is safe.

actionType.description: Action name or id the step uses, e.g. "Click".

object.description: Object name or id the step uses.

parameter.description: A parameter the step uses, by name.

all.description: Required to patch EVERY step when no other criterion is given.

unique.description: true makes this the object's DEFAULT locator (the one the UI marks as default and the executor uses first); only one default exists — it is cleared on the others. object_update also has `defaultLocator` (by name).

from.description: Parameter the step uses now (name, or numeric id).

to.description: Parameter to use instead (name; created when missing).

value.description: The new parameter's test-data value for this step.

through.description: Copy steps n..through (required when step n opens an IF / loop / function block).

at.description: 1-based position the copy takes (default: end of the test case).

tools.name: tc_draft_get
tools.description: Fetch a draft by id: readable steps table, validation summary, and the neutral TestCase.

tools.name: tc_draft_discard
tools.description: Delete an in-memory draft. Nothing was ever persisted, so there is nothing else to undo.

tools.name: tc_draft_open
tools.description: Show this draft in the product's real editor. Prefers the local agent's own native window when the agent is running; otherwise returns a link to open. The draft rides in the URL fragment -- nothing is uploaded, no backend call is made.

tools.name: tc_edit_open
tools.description:
One-shot: hydrate an EXISTING test case as a draft, open it in the desktop TC-viewer window, and bind a live-edit session so subsequent tc_draft_update calls stream the changes into the window in real time (TC_EDIT_RESYNC on each op batch, per plan/tc-edit-live-protocol.md). ⚠️ THIS OPENS THE DESKTOP RECORDER/VIEWER WINDOW (scrcpy / SCRPY). Use it ONLY when the user explicitly wants to WATCH the edits live or asks to open the test case in the viewer. For a plain prompt like "add a step to TC N at step 3", "remove step 2", "change step 3" do NOT use it — call journal_modify({ tcId, ops:[{ op:"add_step", at, step }] }), which edits the saved test case directly with no window.

Returns { draftId, sessionId, tcId }. Follow up with tc_draft_update({ draftId, ops }) for edits and tc_save({ draftId }) to persist. Requires a live connection (qa_connect); the desktop app must be running on the same machine or the window-open call silently no-ops (the draft still mutates correctly — only the live view is lost).

tcId.description: The existing test-case id to open for editing.

hashRoute.description: Optional Angular hash route override, e.g. "#/user/testcase/details/593". Defaults to "#/user/testcase/details/<numericTcId>" (matches the browser UI route). Pass this only if the product's testcase-details route differs from the default.

baseUrl.description: sqa-ui origin (defaults to whatever the desktop app is configured with).

accessToken.description: Bearer token forwarded to the desktop window for API calls.

tools.name: tc_record_append
tools.description:
Start a live-browser recording session whose captured steps stream into the tc-viewer window bound by an earlier `tc_edit_open`. Each user interaction becomes a TC_EDIT_INSERT event in the editor. Returns instructions the model must follow (this tool itself does not touch the driver):
  1. `core_activate_technology({ technology:"WEB", mcpTcEditSessionId, testcaseName })` — starts      the browser and binds captures to this window. The response `structuredContent.sessionId` is      the RECORDING session id — remember it for step 3.
  2. Use `web_*` tools to drive the browser. Every captured step shows up live in the editor.
  3. When done, `tc_record_stop({ draftId, recordingSessionId })` reads the recording journal      and appends the captured steps to the draft. Then `tc_save({ draftId })` to persist.

A DESKTOP test case gets a desktop guide instead: technology "DESKTOP", `desktop_launch_application({ app_path })` first, then `desktop_snapshot` + `desktop_*` verbs.

The draft must have been opened via `tc_edit_open` first — its stored sessionId is what binds the recorder to the correct window.

tools.name: tc_record_stop
tools.description:
Read the recording journal for a session and add each captured step to the draft as an `add_step` op. Pairs with `tc_record_append`. Follow with `tc_save({ draftId })` to persist.

CAVEAT: The recording journal is process-scoped and may contain steps from earlier recordings in the same Java-server process. Pass `fromIndex` to skip the first N steps if the journal accumulated prior state — usually the count of steps recorded before `tc_record_append` was called.

fromIndex.description: Optional: skip the first N steps in the journal (defaults to 0 = take all).

tools.name: tc_suggest_functions
tools.description: Call this RIGHT AFTER a recording finishes (before asking the user to save). It compares the recorded steps with the project's existing reusable functions and returns the groups of steps that already exist as a function. If it returns matches, show them to the user and ASK which function(s) to replace (all / some / none) — do not decide for them. Read-only: nothing changes. Pass EXACTLY ONE of `sessionId` (live/finished recording), `draftId`, or `tcId` (already saved).

tcId.description: A saved test case id or business key. Matched on step IDs (actionId/objectId/stepType/technologyType + parameter names), not on display names.

versionId.description: For tcId only: which version's steps to match (an id from the TC's versions[]). Omit for the TC's currently-selected version; on a multi-version TC ASK the user first.

minConfidence.description: For tcId only. 'exact' (default) = same action/element AND the same parameter names; 'strong' also accepts the same action/element with a different parameter set (a re-parameterised copy of the flow).

tools.name: tc_suggest_function_groups
tools.description: THE post-recording step: call this as soon as a recording finishes and BEFORE asking the user to save. It returns BOTH kinds of suggestion in one answer: `replace` — blocks of recorded steps that already exist as a reusable function (offer to swap them for a call to that function), and `create` — contiguous blocks that are good candidates for a NEW reusable function (offer to extract them). Read-only: nothing is created, replaced or saved. Show both lists and ASK the user per block: create as a new function (ask for the name) / replace with the existing FN-x / keep as recorded. Apply AFTER the test case is saved (tc_steps_to_function with replaceInSource:true, or tc_replace_with_functions). Pass EXACTLY ONE of `sessionId` (a finished recording), `draftId`, or `tcId` (already saved).

tcId.description: A saved test case id or business key.

versionId.description: For tcId only: which version to analyse (an id from the TC versions[]).

groupSize.description: Target steps per proposed new function. Default 6, minimum 3.

tools.name: tc_replace_with_functions
tools.description: After the user has chosen (from tc_suggest_functions) which functions to use, swap the matching steps of an already-saved test case for a call to each chosen function. Use this when the user saved from the recorder window; if the recording is not saved yet, pass the choice to tc_save instead. `functionIds` = the user's picks; omit for all matches. The replaced steps' own testdata is dropped and the function's default iterations are used. ONLY call after the user said yes.

tcId.description: Saved test case id or business key.

functionIds.description: Function ids to apply (from tc_suggest_functions). Omit = all matches.

replace.description: Explicit picks: replace exactly these seqs with these functions, skipping the matcher. Takes precedence over functionIds. This is the "use FN-12 for steps 3-6" path.

stepSeqs.description: The `seq`s of the test case steps to swap for this function — use this when the user names the function AND the range. Must be contiguous.

versionId.description: Version to edit (an id from the TC versions[]). Omit for the current version.

tools.name: tc_save
tools.description:
Persist a test case to the connected product. Pass EXACTLY ONE of:
  • `draftId` — validate and save a draft (create, or update when the draft carries an id).
  • `sessionId` — save a LIVE/RECENT recording by asking the /mcp-recorder window to click its OWN Save button. This is the exact-parity path: the recorder editor saves the steps, objects, parameters, control flow, functions, API popup values and title/module/story that the user is looking at, including edits made in the window. The recorder window must be open; it stays open for review after saving. Returns the created test case id + deep link.
Requires a live connection (qa_connect).
EXCEPTION — API recordings: after the LAST `api_send_request`, call this ONCE with the sessionId WITHOUT asking, so the recorded API test case is persisted and searchable immediately (the user must not have to click Send and Save first). Only once per recording; never per request.
⚠️ OTHERWISE CALL ONLY ON AN EXPLICIT USER SAVE INSTRUCTION (e.g. "save it", "save this", "persist it"). RECORDING or AUTHORING a test case is NOT a save instruction; neither is the user approving the content ("looks good", "nice"). After a recording/draft finishes, SHOW the steps and ASK — do NOT auto-save. When unsure whether a reply meant save, ASK rather than saving. Never save a recording TWICE (UI Save + tc_save): if the user already clicked Save in the recorder, treat it as done.

draftId.description: Draft id from tc_draft_create / tc_draft_open. Omit when saving a live recording.

sessionId.description: Recording session id from core_activate_technology (or core_active_recordings). Saves via the recorder window's own Save button.

allowDuplicate.description: Set true ONLY after the user confirms they want a new test case with the same name as an existing one. Default: a new test case whose name already exists is saved as name_1, name_2, ….

replaceWithFunctions.description: Function reuse. Before saving, the steps are compared with the project's existing functions. If some already exist as a function and this is OMITTED, the tool does NOT save — it returns the matches and you MUST ASK the user "replace with the existing function(s)?". Then call again with true (replace ALL matches), an array of function ids (replace only those — the user picked some), or false (save as recorded, the normal flow). Never choose for the user. No matches → saves normally and this is ignored. tc_suggest_functions shows the same matches right after recording.

copyTestdataFrom.description: Optional source TC id (or TC code). After the recording is saved, copy that TC's default-iteration testdata onto the new test case, matching parameters BY NAME. Use this when converting a manual TC (tc_automate) so the converted TC keeps the manual testdata instead of the values typed during recording. Omit for a normal recording.

tools.name: tc_automate
tools.description: Read an EXISTING MANUAL test case and return a recording guide the model uses to drive a live recording via the connected agent's granular tools (web_launch_application, web_snapshot, web_click, web_enter_text, …, core_close_session). The Electron recorder window opens automatically on web_launch_application; each captured step streams into it. The user reviews and clicks Save in the recorder — that CREATES A NEW automated test case (via POST /tm/testcase); the source manual TC is left untouched. Pass `url` unless the manual steps already contain one, and `extra` for credentials / data / what to assert. Read-only from MCP: this tool composes text, it never writes. Requires a live connection.

tcId.description: The manual test case id (or business key TC_123) to automate.

url.description: Starting URL for the recording (the app under test).

extra.description: Extra guidance for the recording: credentials, data, assertions.

app_path.description: DESKTOP test cases only (tcType DESKTOP): the full path of the application's .exe. A DESKTOP test case needs no `url`; its guide uses the desktop_* tools.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the projects visible to the current connection — id, name and counts. Use this to resolve a project NAME to its id (e.g. before qa_switch_project when the user names a project). Requires a live connection.

tools.name: tc_list
tools.description: List or search EXISTING TEST CASES (TC_* ids) in the connected product. NOT for reusable functions: if the user asks for functions, FN_*, the function library, or reusable steps, use `list_functions` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "test case", "TC", "TC_", "scenario", "script". Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Returns a summary list — id, title, technology, execution type, step count. Use `tc_get` to read one in full. Read-only, product-neutral. When presenting this as a table, label the columns "ID" and "Name" — the underlying fields are literally named `code`/`title`, but that's internal wire terminology, not what to show the user.

status.description: Filter by status. Walnut only — SimplifyQA test cases have no status field (use `reviewApproveStatus` or a custom field via sqa_query).

createdBy.description: Numeric userId of the creator. Pass "me" to filter by the current caller (needs QA_MCP_USER_ID for API-key auth). Resolve names to ids via list_users first.

updatedBy.description: Numeric userId of the last updater. Pass "me" for the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

storyId.description: Only test cases tagged to this user story (id or business key, e.g. US_123).

moduleId.description: Only test cases filed under this module (id or business key, e.g. MO_12). SimplifyQA only — ignored elsewhere.

obsolete.description: True → only obsolete TCs; false → only non-obsolete. Omit to include both. The response summary always reports how many of the returned rows are obsolete.

filters.description: Extra raw column filters for project-configured columns with no dedicated parameter above (e.g. custom fields) — use the field's backend key as `column`. SimplifyQA test cases have no priority/status/stepCount columns.

column.description: Backend field name to filter on, e.g. "priority", "moduleId", "customFields.Team".

value.description: Exact-match value (or substring when `regEx` is true).

regEx.description: Substring/regex match instead of exact equality.

output.description: How to return a LARGE result. Omit it: when more than 100 test cases match, the tool returns ONLY the total count + the options and you must ASK the user. 'xlsx' = write ALL matches to an .xlsx file (use directly when the user asked for Excel / a download — no need to ask). 'first100' = show exactly the first 100 inline. At 100 or fewer matches results are shown inline either way. Ignored when `limit`/`offset` is passed (an explicit page).

tools.name: tc_get
tools.description:
Read a single EXISTING test case in full — metadata plus its steps as a readable table — from the connected product. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). `id` accepts the product's id or business key. Product-neutral: same shape on any connected product.

VERSIONS: SimplifyQA TCs can have multiple versions, each with its own steps. When the TC has more than one version and `versionId` is omitted, this tool REFUSES and lists the available versions — ASK the user which one to read, then call again with `versionId`. Pass `versionId: ''` (empty string) to accept the TC's currently-selected version. Single- version TCs are read directly. Providers without versioning (Walnut) ignore `versionId`.

id.description: The test case id (or business key) to read.

versionId.description: Version to read (an id from the TC's `versions[]`). Omit to trigger the ASK-user prompt when the TC has multiple versions. Pass '' (empty string) to accept the TC's currently-selected version without prompting.

tools.name: tc_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an existing test case in the connected product. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: call once with just `tcId` to preview the target (title + step count) and get a warning; then call again with `{ tcId, confirm: true }` to actually delete. Refuses to delete without `confirm:true`. `tcId` accepts the product's id or business key. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Product-neutral.

tcId.description: The test case id (or business key) to delete.

confirm.description: Set to true on the SECOND call to actually delete.

tools.name: tc_clone
tools.description:
FOR TEST CASES ONLY. NOT for reusable functions: if the user names an `FN_*` key or asks to clone a function, use `fn_clone` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "test case", "TC", "TC_", "scenario", "script".

Save an existing test case as a NEW test case (new TC id) in the SAME project + module. Mirrors the FE in-editor "Save as new TC" dialog (operation: SAVEASNEWTC). Clones ONE source version — pass `sourceVersionId` to pick which; defaults to the TC's currently selected version. `tcId` accepts the numeric id or business key (`TC_*`).

`newName` is REQUIRED — backend rejects an empty name on SAVEASNEWTC.

TESTDATA — TWO-STEP: call once WITHOUT `tdCopy` to get the "Copy Test Data" prompt and confirm with the user; then call again with `tdCopy` set. Mirrors the FE's "COPY TEST DATA" modal (Cancel = false, Confirm = true). The tool REFUSES to clone until `tdCopy` is passed — the prompt step is not skippable.

`tdCopy:true` clones the source version's testdata iterations across every environment. `tdCopy:false` copies only the column STRUCTURE — one empty iteration (`ITR-1`) per environment; cells fall back to each parameter's project-level `defaultValue` if any.

Requires a live connection.

tcId.description: The source test case id or business key (e.g. TC_123).

newName.description: Name for the new test case (required by backend).

tools.name: tc_steps_to_function
tools.description:
Take a subset of the steps on an EXISTING test case and save them as a new reusable function (SimplifyQA STEPSTOFN operation). Mirrors the FE "Save as function" modal. Steps are picked by their current `seq`, resequenced 1..N in the new function, and filed under `moduleId`. `tcId` accepts the numeric id or business key (TC_123). Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

CALL THIS when the user says things like "save these steps as a function", "convert the first N steps to a function", "extract these steps into a function". Show the steps of the TC first (via tc_get) so the user can confirm which `seq`s to extract, and ASK the user which module to file the new function under — call `list_modules` if the module id is not known.

VERSIONS: SimplifyQA TCs can have multiple versions with DIFFERENT step counts/content. When the TC has more than one version and `versionId` is omitted, this tool REFUSES and lists the available versions — ASK the user which version's steps to convert, read that version's steps with tc_get({ id, versionId }) to confirm the `seq`s, then call this tool again with the SAME `versionId`. Pass `versionId: ''` to accept the TC's currently-selected version without prompting. Single-version TCs are used directly.

`executionType` forces every picked step into the AUTOMATION or MANUAL bucket; omit to split by each step's own executionType (function will be DUO if both are present).

TESTDATA: iterations from the source TC version are copied to the new function by default. The backend prunes them to only the parameters the extracted steps reference (via key-based matching in tcfn.service.js `compareDatas` `isStepsToFn` mode), across every environment the source version has. Pass `copyTestData: false` if you explicitly want a bare function.

REPLACE-IN-SOURCE: pass `replaceInSource: true` to also splice a FUNCTION + FUNCTION_END pair back into the source TC in place of the extracted steps (mirrors the FE "Save & Replace" button). The extracted rows are soft-deleted; the backend automatically drops any testdata columns those steps owned and injects an FN cell (with the FN's per-env default iteration) into every TC iteration row. Requires a contiguous `stepSeqs` range and refuses picks that cross control-flow (IF/WHILE/FOR/DO) or nested FUNCTION brackets, and DUO/SYNCON TCs — those are v2 cases.

FAILURE MODE with replaceInSource: if the FN is created but the follow-up PUT fails, the error surfaces the new fn id + version id so you can retry or delete the phantom function.

tools.name: journal_modify
tools.description:
Apply granular edits to an EXISTING test case and persist them, opening the result in the test-case editor. Use journal_grep first to see the numbered steps, then pass ops (numbers are from that view, 1-based):
  • add_step / update_step / remove_step / move_step — edit individual steps
  • duplicate_step { n, through?, at? } — copy the WHOLE step (parameters, values, object, flags, settings) to the end or to `at`; use this for "add the same step again", not add_step. `through` is required when n opens an IF / loop / function block.
  • update_steps { where, patch } — one patch for EVERY matching step ("skip every step that uses X"); where: numbers, from/to, stepType, actionType, object, descriptionContains, parameter, or all:true
  • a step patch may carry swapParams [{ from, to, value? }] to replace one parameter with another in the same slot (recordedParam only adds)
  • add_assertions { n, assertions:[{ path, condition, expectedValue }] } — APPEND response assertions to an EXISTING API step (path: statusCode | responseTime | responseSize | $.body.x | $.headers.Name). The request, object, action, parameters and existing assertions are untouched — use this for "add only the assertion to step N".
  • update_step patch.api is MERGED into the saved API request (add an assertion: api.addAssertions [{ path, condition, expectedValue }]; api.assertions replaces the list) — edit an API step with this, never remove_step + add_step
  • wrap_in_loop { from, to, condition?, maxIterations? } — wrap steps from..to in a while loop
  • wrap_in_if   { from, to, condition? } — wrap steps from..to in an if block
  • insert_nested { at?, tcId, name? } — insert an existing test case as a nested step (reuse)
For a test case backed by a recording journal the journal is kept in sync (so healer / re-record stay consistent); others edit the persisted steps. NOTE: adding a brand-new INTERACTION step (click/type on a new element) via add_step has no captured locator, so it is a manual/non-executable step — unless you give it an object: pass objectRef { id } or { name } to reuse an existing object from the repository, or { name, locators:[{ name, value }] } to create one. A step that needs NO element — e.g. Minimum Wait — needs none. Use add_step { at?, step: { actionType:"Minimum Wait", stepType, description, value? } } — `at` (alias `seq`) is the 1-based position the new step takes; it is inserted there DIRECTLY (the recorder window does not open) and the other steps just shift down. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: sqa_query
tools.description:
THE ONLY READ TOOL ON SIMPLIFYQA. Use it for EVERY fetch / query / list / search / get / read / count request. The old per-collection read tools (tc_list, tc_get, story_list, story_get, epic_list, feature_list, list_modules, list_functions, suite_list, list_users, object_list, defect_list, task_list, list_releases, list_sprints, journal_grep, ...) are NOT registered on a SimplifyQA connection — do not look for them and do not invent one.

FLOW: (1) `op:"catalog"` (optionally with a collection) to see descriptions/fields/relations, (2) `op:"search"` for a list or `op:"get"` for one row, (3) `op:"related"` to follow a FK (story → testcases, testcase → defects, suite → runs, module → testcases, ...). For "how many" use `op:"count"` (same `where`), and add `groupBy` for a breakdown ("defects by severity").

RULES: every search injects `deleted:false` and the active project; deleted rows are never returned. Unknown fields/operators are rejected locally (the backend silently returns 0 rows for unknown columns). `priority`/`status` do NOT exist on SimplifyQA test cases — use `reviewApproveStatus` or a custom field.

CUSTOM FIELDS: `op:"custom_fields"` returns label → key → `customFields.<key>`; then pass the label as `field` with `custom:true` in `where` (or resolve one with `name`).

EXAMPLES:
- "list API test cases in module 46" → `{ op:"search", collection:"testcases", where:[{field:"tcType",op:"eq",value:"API"},{field:"moduleId",op:"eq",value:46}] }`
- "defects for TC 684" → `{ op:"related", collection:"testcases", id:"684", relation:"defects" }`
- "latest run of suite 120 + steps" → `{ op:"search", collection:"executions", where:[{field:"executionTypeId",op:"eq",value:120},{field:"type",op:"eq",value:"SUITE"}], sort:[{field:"id",dir:"desc"}], limit:1 }` then `{ op:"get", collection:"executions", id:"<runId>" }`
- "testcases where SEVERITY is High" → `{ op:"search", collection:"testcases", where:[{field:"SEVERITY",custom:true,op:"contains",value:"High"}] }`
- "releases / sprints in ALL my projects" → `{ op:"search", collection:"releases", allProjects:true }` and `{ op:"search", collection:"sprints", allProjects:true }` — do NOT qa_switch_project through each project. Release rows carry `projectIds`; sprint rows carry `releaseId`.

TIP: `dryRun:true` returns the compiled `searchFields` payload without making the HTTP call.

op.description: Operation to run. "count" returns how many rows match (with `groupBy`, per value).

groupBy.description: For op:"count": the field to break the count down by (e.g. "state", "severity", "ownerId", "tcType").

includeHidden.description: Include rows hidden by default (obsolete test cases). Naming the field in `where` does the same.

allVersions.description: Stories/epics: return every version row instead of one row per item.

collection.description: Collection name or alias (testcases, tc, stories, defects, executions, ...). Required except for catalog.

where.description: Filters, an ARRAY of { field, op?, value }. Combined with AND unless a filter sets condition:"or". Example: [{ field:"name", op:"contains", value:"login" }].

field.description: Field key for the collection (e.g. moduleId, state, userstoryId). For a custom field, pass its label here and set custom:true.

op.description: Filter operator. Default: "in" for array values, otherwise "eq". "contains" is a case-insensitive substring (the backend escapes regex specials).

value.description: Filter value. Use an array for in/not_in.

custom.description: Resolve `field` against the collection custom fields (match by label or key) and compile it to customFields.<key>.

condition.description: Combine with the other filters using AND (default) or OR.

select.description: Fields to return. Use ["*"] for the full row. Defaults to the collection summary projection.

offset.description: Row offset (not a page number — the engine sets skipStartIndex).

relation.description: Relation name from the catalog — required for op:"related".

tools.description:
READ-ONLY preflight for recording: resolves the role the connected user holds in a project and that role's privilege keys, then says whether recording is allowed there. Answers the three failure modes BEFORE anything is created: invalid/expired token, no role in the project, or a role missing a write the recorder needs (add_testcase / add_parameter / add_object, plus mobile/mainframe/cloud integration keys for those technologies).

Returns verdict ok | no-role | missing-privileges | invalid-token, the role name, the full privilege list, a `can` summary, and the exact keys to ask an admin for. The product agent runs the same check inside core_activate_technology, so you never need to call this first — call it when you want to warn the user, or to explain a refusal.

technology.description: Check the extra privileges this recording technology needs (mobile/mainframe integration keys). Default: WEB.

provider.description: Device provider for ANDROID/IOS (local|emulator|simplifyqa|lambdatest|browserstack|saucelabs) — cloud providers also need allow_cloud_integration.

need.description: Extra privilege keys to verify, e.g. ["add_userstory"].

GET-OR-CREATE by NAME (case-insensitive): if an object with the same name already exists, this reuses it — updating its locators in place if they differ — instead of creating a duplicate. Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

tools.description:
READ-ONLY. Show every object (locator-bound UI element) referenced by an EXISTING test case's steps — id, name, and which step(s) use it. This tool NEVER deletes, updates, or creates anything, no matter what; it only reads. A referenced object id that no longer resolves (deleted, or never existed) is reported CLEARLY as "MISSING" — never silently dropped from the list or shown as if nothing were wrong.

VERSIONS: SimplifyQA TCs can have multiple versions with different step/object bindings — when the TC has more than one version and `versionId` is omitted, this tool REFUSES and lists the available versions (same rule as tc_get) — ASK the user which one, then call again with `versionId`. Pass versionId: '' to accept the current version. Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

tools.name: parameter_update
tools.description:
Edit a PARAMETER itself in the project - not a step's use of it. Typical: "make task_doc a Runtime parameter" (a store slot written by a Read action must be Runtime), or change its default value / description. Local <-> Runtime only: Global parameters are encrypted and shared and are not edited here.

IMPACT: the change applies to EVERY test case that uses this parameter. So the call is a preview until you pass `confirm: true` - show the user what will change and that it affects every use, then call again with confirm. The parameter is re-read after the update and the call REFUSES if the change did not take. Requires a live connection.

parameter.description: The parameter's exact name (case-insensitive) or numeric id.

confirm.description: Must be true to apply. Without it the call only describes what would change.

tools.name: object_update
tools.description:
Update an object in the shared Object Repository — rename it, change its description, set which parameter(s) it is bound to, move it to a different module, and/or fix locator values directly (e.g. a stale `data-test` attribute). Any combination of these can be set in ONE call when the user states them together. `locators` UPSERTS by strategy name: an entry matching an EXISTING locator name updates its value/unique in place, everything else on the object is untouched, and a name with no existing match is added as a NEW locator — you do not need to resupply the full locator set.

DEFAULT LOCATOR: to make a locator the object's DEFAULT (the one the UI marks as default and the executor uses first — "make it default"), pass `defaultLocator: "<locator name>"`, e.g. add an xpath with `locators: [{ name: "xpath", value: "//input[@id='u']" }]` AND `defaultLocator: "xpath"` in one call. It can also name a locator already on the object (no need to resend its value). Only one default exists — it is cleared on the others. The result is re-read and the call REFUSES if the default did not take.

`parameterNames` REPLACES the object's full parameter binding with these (resolved by exact name, case-insensitive) — pass the CURRENT set plus the new one if the user means "also bind" rather than "replace"; read the object first (object_get) if you need to know the current bindings. `moduleName` takes the module's NAME, never an id — it is resolved automatically. Both REFUSE clearly (naming the bad value and the valid options) if the name doesn't match anything, rather than silently saving nothing.

The object's TYPE (technology) and TEMPLATE ID are NOT editable here — they are structural (they determine which attribute set is even valid) and stay whatever they already are; changing either means creating a new object, not updating this one. Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

name.description: New display name for the object.

parameterNames.description: REPLACES the object's bound parameters with these, resolved by exact name (case-insensitive). Pass the full desired set, not just the one being added.

moduleName.description: Move the object to this module, by NAME (resolved automatically — never pass an id).

locators.description: Locators to upsert by name, e.g. [{ name: "data-test", value: "123456" }] to fix one attribute — every other locator on the object is left as-is.

unique.description: true makes this the object's DEFAULT locator (the one the UI marks as default and the executor uses first); only one default exists — it is cleared on the others. object_update also has `defaultLocator` (by name).

defaultLocator.description: NAME of the locator to make the object's DEFAULT, e.g. "xpath" — one you add in `locators` in this same call, or one already on the object. Use this whenever the user says "make it default".

tools.name: object_delete
tools.description: Delete an object from the shared Object Repository. TWO-STEP CONFIRM, REQUIRED even for a single object: call once with just `id` to preview it (name/type + how many test cases, functions, or workflows still reference it); then call again with `{ id, confirm: true }` to actually delete. NEVER call this with confirm:true on the first call, and NEVER call it at all unless the user's own words asked to DELETE — a request to list, show, or read objects (object_list / object_get / "show me the objects in this test case") is NEVER a reason to call this tool. DEPENDENCY-CHECKED: if the object is still referenced by any test case, function, or workflow, the delete is REFUSED at confirm time too — it reports what still uses it instead of silently breaking those. Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

confirm.description: Set to true on the SECOND call to actually delete. Omit (or false) to preview first.

tools.name: story_sync_testcases
tools.description:
Compare a user STORY against every test case linked to it (via storyRef) and return a structured, ORDERED plan for bringing them up to date.

MANUAL test cases → textual drift (ac_added / ac_reworded / ac_removed / step_stale) and the exact draft ops (add_step / update_step / remove_step).
AUTOMATION test cases → `action: "rerecord"` (or `"up-to-date"`) plus the recording brief: the acceptance criteria to cover, story/module ids, current steps and testdata seeds. An automated TC cannot be re-texted — it must be re-recorded.

HOW TO APPLY (one item at a time, in plan order — never in parallel):
  MANUAL item:
    1. tc_draft_from_tc({ tcId })
    2. tc_draft_update({ draftId, ops: item.proposedOps })
    3. tc_save_as_new_version({ tcId, fromDraftId: draftId })   ← new version (v1.0 → v2.0)
  OBSOLETE item (action === "obsolete") — the scenario this TC tested was REMOVED from the story
    and NO step matches any current AC:
    ASK the user, then journal_modify({ tcId, ops: [{ op: "set_meta", patch: { obsolete: true } }] }).
    Do NOT strip its steps (that leaves an empty, still-active TC) and do NOT delete it.
  PARTIAL removal — only SOME steps belonged to the removed scenario:
    item.proposedOps carries ONE bulk remove_steps { numbers:[11,12,13,14,15] }; apply the MANUAL
    item steps 1-3 above. The result is a NEW VERSION without those steps (v1.0 keeps them).
    NEVER obsolete a partially-affected TC.
  AUTOMATION item (action === "rerecord"):
    1. ASK the user AI-only or Hybrid, then
       core_activate_technology({ technology, testcaseId: item.testCaseId, versionName: item.nextVersionName, testcaseName: item.title, userstoryId: item.brief.userstoryId, moduleId: item.brief.moduleId, recordingMode, recordingModeAskedUser })
       The recorder window opens on THAT test case (details + versions, steps cleared) and
       shows the pending version in the version dropdown (v1.0 → v2.0, v2.0 → v3.0).
    2. Record the brief.acceptanceCriteria end-to-end (web: web_launch_application → web_snapshot → web_click / web_enter_text / web_validate_text …).
       (desktop: desktop_launch_application → desktop_snapshot → desktop_click / desktop_enter_text / desktop_validate_text …; the launch is still the first step.)
    3. SAVE — click Save in the recorder window, OR tc_save({ sessionId }) (it clicks that same
       button). Either one writes the re-recorded flow as a NEW VERSION of the SAME TC (story,
       module, suite and history preserved) with the recorded test-data formulas.
       Do NOT use tc_draft_from_journal / tc_save_as_new_version on this flow — that would save twice.
  In-place editing is available with `versionStrategy: "in-place"` (same ops, tc_save instead of a new version) — use it only when the user explicitly does not want a new version.

Report-only: this tool writes nothing itself. Pass `testCaseIds` to limit the scan; otherwise the tool walks listTestCases and filters by storyRef (bounded by `scanLimit`, default 200). Test cases that are ALREADY obsolete are skipped (reason "already_obsolete"), so a second run after applying the plan only shows what is still left to do. Requires a live connection.

scope.description: Which linked test cases to plan for. Default "both" (manual drift + automation re-record plan).

versionStrategy.description: How a MANUAL update is written: "new" (default) = new version (v1.0 → v2.0) preserving history; "in-place" = overwrite the current version.

sensitivity.description: Match-strictness for AC↔step overlap. strict=more drift flagged, loose=less. Default normal.

scanLimit.description: Cap on how many TCs to fetch when `testCaseIds` is omitted. Default 200.

includeTestData.description: Include the automation brief's testdata seeds (default true; costs one extra read per automation TC). Set false for a fast check.
