tools.description: PATCH an existing USER STORY — pass only the fields to change plus `updateVersion` (optimistic concurrency, from the last story_get). Accepts id or business key (US_123). Pass `acceptanceCriteria` as a newline-separated string when replacing AC lines.

tools.name: backlog_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Delete ONE epic, feature, user story, defect or task. `ref` is the item's NAME, business key (EP_12, FT_3, US_5, DF_7 …) or numeric id — resolved here, the user never supplies an internal id. TWO-STEP: call WITHOUT `confirm` to get a preview (what will be deleted + anything that depends on it); show it to the user and ASK; only then call again with `confirm:true`. An item that still has dependents (an epic with features/stories, a feature/story with children or test cases, a defect with test cases/tasks) is REFUSED with the blockers listed — nothing cascades. An ambiguous name lists the matches and deletes nothing. Needs the user's delete permission; no agent required. Requires a live connection.

kind.description: Which kind of item to delete.

ref.description: Name, business key (EP_/FT_/US_/DF_…) or numeric id of the item.

confirm.description: Set true ONLY after the user has seen the preview and explicitly confirmed the delete.

tools.name: failure_analysis
tools.description:
Analyse FAILED executions on SimplifyQA — test case, suite or execution plan. Pass `code` = TC-123 / SU-123 / PL-123 (PL = execution plan) for its LATEST execution (standalone test case run; parent execution for a suite or plan), or `executionId` (number or EX code) for ONLY that execution; both together analyse that code inside that execution. A test case gets every iteration; a suite or plan gets every failed test case with all of its failed iterations, grouped by cause.

The result starts with an ANALYSIS CARD (tables: "Why … failed", "Failed test cases" with Report Step No. and Test case step, each failed iteration). YOUR REPLY MUST START WITH THAT CARD EXACTLY AS RETURNED — same tables and rows, not reworded or summarised — and then add Why / Fix per cause from the evidence that follows it.

code.description: TC-123, SU-123 or PL-123 (execution plan). Without executionId, its latest execution is analysed.

executionId.description: Execution id or EX code. When set, only this execution is analysed.

runId.description: Same as executionId (kept for older calls).

tcId.description: Test case id — same as code TC-<id>.

suiteId.description: Suite id — same as code SU-<id>.

maxLogLines.description: Cap logs per step — the lines nearest the failure are kept (default 30).

includeImages.description: Return the failure screenshot of each top cause group as an inline image (default true, max 5). Set false for text and links only.

tools.name: cloud_runners
tools.description: List the cloud runner VMs registered to the connected project and which are online. Use this to show the user the cloud options, or to pick a specific runner id for tc_run. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: local_agents
tools.description: List the LOCAL agent(s) registered from THIS machine — the desktop agent running on the box this MCP is on. Use for a LOCAL tc_run / suite_run. There is exactly one desktop agent per machine, so this is 0 or 1 row: empty means no agent is registered from this box (start the SimplifyQA desktop agent, or use mode:'remote' to dispatch to a teammate's). Use `remote_agents` for the other registered machines. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: remote_agents
tools.description: List the LOCAL agents registered on OTHER machines (teammates' boxes) — the pool a REMOTE run dispatches to. Use to pick an `agentId` for a REMOTE tc_run / suite_run. Excludes this machine's own agent (that's `local_agents`). REMOTE dispatches to a specific teammate's registered desktop agent through the SimplifyQA queue; the picked agent's browsers / adb devices are what actually execute. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: mobile_list_devices
tools.description: List MOBILE devices available to the project — union of the LOCAL roster (real devices + emulators/simulators registered via the desktop agent, from `/tm/mobileDevices/search`) and the CLOUD roster (whichever farm the project has integrated: LambdaTest / BrowserStack / SauceLabs / SimplifyQA Device Farm — the first non-empty one wins, matching the UI's single-provider-per-project model). Use before `tc_run` for an ANDROID or IOS test case to pick a `deviceId` (and read `deviceType` + `cloudDeviceType` off the same row). The `active` flag on local rows is last-known: stale by design (the SQA backend writes it when the desktop agent connects/disconnects, and a 7s-stale cron flips it back); a device the user just plugged in may still read `active:false` here. Cloud rows don't carry `active` — cloud farms are always assumed reachable. Requires a live connection.

platform.description: Which mobile platform to list devices for.

tools.name: tc_run
tools.description:
★ ORDER OF QUESTIONS (STRICT — applies whether you ask one at a time OR bundle several into a single message): when → mode → release → sprint → version → environment → browser/device → schedule fields → agent. Ask in THIS order, always — never schema-declaration order, never refusal-arrival order, never a 'natural UI' order (release first is WRONG). Skip a step only when the flag below says it's skippable (sprint when release='', version when TC has one version, browser vs. device by TC type). ★

Execute ONE existing test case in the connected product. ASK the user for EVERY field the Execute dialog asks — never assume — in this DEPENDENCY ORDER: (0) if a previous run in this session left a config for the project, the tool refuses first asking `reuseConfig` (true=merge remembered mode/release/sprint/env/browser/agent, false=start fresh); (1) `when` immediate/schedule, (2) `mode` local/remote/cloud, (3) `releaseId` (from list_releases; pass '' to skip — no release), (4) `sprintId` (from list_sprints; skipped entirely when releaseId=''), (5) `versionId` (from tc_get's `versions[]`; pass '' for current), (6) `environment` (from tc_list_environments), (7) FOR WEB TCs: `browser`; FOR ANDROID/IOS TCs: `deviceType` + `deviceId` (via `mobile_list_devices`), (8) for a schedule the start time + recurrence (ASK — Once / Every 5 Minutes / Hourly / Daily / Weekly / Monthly, never default) + end date + timezone, (9) THEN offer the eligible agent/runner and pass the pick. IF YOU BATCH SEVERAL REFUSED FIELDS INTO ONE AskUserQuestion, ORDER the questions EXACTLY as above (when → mode → release → sprint → version → environment → browser/device → schedule fields → agent) — never in schema order or refusal order. `mode` decides WHERE it runs:
  • 'local' — THIS machine's desktop agent (its own browser). Call `local_agents` (0 or 1 row per box). For when:'immediate' the tool first probes the desktop agent (:4040) and refuses cleanly if it's not up. Omit `agentId` to auto-pick this machine's agent (or pass it explicitly — must be this machine's row). For when:'schedule' `agentId` is REQUIRED.
  • 'remote' — ANOTHER registered machine's desktop agent (a teammate's box). Call `remote_agents` and OFFER the list; `agentId` is REQUIRED (no auto-pick across boxes). For when:'immediate' only ONLINE remote agents are eligible; for when:'schedule' ANY remote agent works (it runs when it fires).
  • 'cloud' — an online cloud runner VM (ONLINE-only whether now or scheduled). Pass `cloudRunnerId` from cloud_runners; for a schedule omit it to let the backend auto-pick a live VM at fire time.
For cloud, if no runner is online it reports that there are no active cloud runners (nothing is run).
NOTE: MANUAL test cases cannot be run or scheduled by an agent — the backend rejects them.

tcId.description: The test case id (or business key) to run.

reuseConfig.description: Set only when the tool refused asking about REUSE. true = merge the previous run's mode/release/sprint/env/browser/agent/runner into any unset field; false = ignore prior config and walk the full cascade. Omit on a first run.

when.description: STEP 1 — when to run. REQUIRED, ASK the user if unstated (the tool refuses when omitted). 'immediate' dispatches now; 'schedule' creates a schedule (needs scheduledFor).

mode.description: STEP 2 — where to run. REQUIRED, ASK the user if unstated.

releaseId.description: STEP 3 — tag the run with a RELEASE (from list_releases). Optional in the UI; pass '' after asking to skip. The tool refuses when undefined so the user is asked.

sprintId.description: STEP 4 — tag the run with a SPRINT (from list_sprints, scoped to release). Only asked when releaseId is non-empty; skipped entirely when releaseId=''. Pass '' after asking to skip.

versionId.description: STEP 5 — override the TC's currently-selected VERSION for this run (an id or name from the TC's `versions[]`). Pass '' to accept the TC's current version.

environment.description: STEP 6 — environment key (from tc_list_environments). ASK the user; the UI marks this required.

browser.description: STEP 7 (WEB TCs) — browser, default 'chromium' (bundled + isolated). Others: 'chrome'/'msedge' (installed channel), 'firefox', 'webkit'. NOTE: a schedule accepts only chromium/msedge/firefox/webkit.

deviceId.description: STEP 7 (ANDROID/IOS TCs) — the target device id. LOCAL: adb serial or emulator name. CLOUD: the marketplace device name. Enumerate with `mobile_list_devices`.

deviceName.description: STEP 7 (ANDROID/IOS TCs) — the human-readable device name (e.g. 'Oppo-Cph2375-Ab1fe936', 'Pixel 7'). Read off the matching row's `displayName` (preferred) or `name` field from `mobile_list_devices`. Shown in the execution report. Auto-resolved from the device roster if omitted.

deviceType.description: STEP 7 (ANDROID/IOS TCs) — the KIND of device the picked `deviceId` is (read off the matching row from `mobile_list_devices`).

cloudDeviceType.description: REQUIRED when `deviceType` is cloud_* — which cloud farm the device came from (read off the matching row's `cloudDeviceType`).

osVersion.description: Optional OS version to stamp on the wire platform object for ANDROID/IOS — read off the matching row from `mobile_list_devices`.

agentId.description: STEP 9 — for local: a credential_id from `local_agents` (must be THIS machine's row; omit to auto-pick). For remote: REQUIRED — a credential_id from `remote_agents`. when:'immediate' → the picked agent must be ONLINE; when:'schedule' → offline OK and `agentId` is REQUIRED for both local and remote.

cloudRunnerId.description: STEP 9 (cloud) — a specific ONLINE runner id (from cloud_runners). For when:'schedule' omit to auto-pick a live VM at fire time.

headless.description: Headless. Defaults: cloud=true, local=false. (Immediate runs only.)

scheduledFor.description: STEP 8 — REQUIRED for when:'schedule'; ISO datetime of the first/only run (e.g. '2026-08-20T09:00:00Z').

scheduleType.description: SCHEDULE STEP — REQUIRED for when:'schedule'; ASK the user explicitly, never assume. The UI's Recurrence choices: 'once', 'every_5_minutes', 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'. Anything but 'once' also needs endDate. ('weekdays' = weekly Mon–Fri, MCP shortcut — don't offer it.)

endDate.description: SCHEDULE STEP — ISO end date; REQUIRED when scheduleType is anything but 'once'. ASK the user.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for a schedule (e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'). Default 'UTC'.

tools.name: suite_run
tools.description:
★ ORDER OF QUESTIONS (STRICT — applies whether you ask one at a time OR bundle several into a single message): when → mode → strategy (serial/parallel, IMMEDIATE runs) → release → sprint → environment → schedule fields → agent. Ask in THIS order, always — never schema-declaration order, never refusal-arrival order, never a 'natural UI' order (release first is WRONG). Skip sprint when release=''. Suites do NOT ask version / browser / device — each TC in the suite carries its own. ★

Execute an existing test SUITE — all its member test cases, in order — in the connected product. ASK the user for EVERY field the UI's Execute-suite dialog asks — never assume — in this DEPENDENCY ORDER: (0) if a previous run in this session left a config for the project, the tool refuses first asking `reuseConfig` (true=merge remembered mode/release/sprint/env/agent, false=start fresh); (1) `when` immediate/schedule, (2) `mode` local/remote/cloud, (3) `strategy` SERIAL/PARALLEL — the UI's PARALLEL/SERIAL radio, shown for LOCAL, REMOTE and CLOUD alike (ask it for an immediate run), (4) `releaseId` (from list_releases; pass '' to skip), (5) `sprintId` (from list_sprints; skipped entirely when releaseId=''), (6) `environment` (from tc_list_environments), (7) for a schedule the start time + recurrence (ASK — Once / Every 5 Minutes / Hourly / Daily / Weekly / Monthly, never default) + end date + timezone, (8) THEN offer the eligible agent/runner. IF YOU BATCH SEVERAL REFUSED FIELDS INTO ONE AskUserQuestion, ORDER the questions EXACTLY as above (when → mode → strategy → release → sprint → environment → schedule fields → agent) — never in schema order or refusal order. UNLIKE `tc_run`, a suite does NOT ask for `versionId` or `browser` — each TC in the suite carries its own pinned version + execution platform (that's what the suite editor picks per row). ★ RECOMMEND PARALLEL when the suite has more than one test case that can run independently (they dispatch concurrently — much faster); recommend SERIAL when the cases must run in order or share state (create → verify → delete, one shared login, a single local browser profile). The UI preselects SERIAL — say WHY you suggest parallel.
`mode` decides WHERE it runs:
  • 'local' — THIS machine's desktop agent. Runs SERIAL or PARALLEL exactly as asked (parallel dispatches each TC as its own child execution). Call `local_agents` (0 or 1 row). For when:'immediate' the tool probes :4040 and refuses if the desktop agent is down. Omit `agentId` to auto-pick this machine's agent; for when:'schedule' `agentId` is REQUIRED.
  • 'remote' — ANOTHER registered machine's desktop agent, SERIAL or PARALLEL as asked. Call `remote_agents`; `agentId` is REQUIRED (no auto-pick). when:'immediate' → ONLINE only; when:'schedule' → offline OK.
  • 'cloud' — online cloud runner VM(s) (ONLINE-only whether now or scheduled). Pass `cloudRunnerId` from cloud_runners; for a schedule omit it to auto-pick a live VM at fire time.
For cloud, if no runner is online it reports that there are no active cloud runners (nothing is run).
NOTE: manual suites go through the same dispatch — the backend stores them as an execution (no agent picks them up until steps are marked from the UI).

suiteId.description: The suite id to run (from suite_list / suite_get).

reuseConfig.description: Set only when the tool refused asking about REUSE. true = merge the previous run's mode/release/sprint/env/browser/agent/runner into any unset field; false = ignore prior config. Omit on a first run.

when.description: STEP 1 — when to run. REQUIRED, ASK the user if unstated.

mode.description: STEP 2 — where to run. REQUIRED, ASK the user if unstated.

releaseId.description: STEP 4 — release from list_releases. ASK the user; pass '' to skip (no release / no sprint asked).

sprintId.description: STEP 5 — sprint from list_sprints (scoped to release). Only asked when releaseId is non-empty; skipped when releaseId=''. Pass '' to skip.

environment.description: STEP 6 — environment key (from tc_list_environments). ASK the user; the UI marks this required for a suite.

browser.description: Optional at the SUITE level — each TC in the suite has its own execution platform (that's the suite-editor pick per row). Provide only to OVERRIDE for every WEB TC. Values: 'chromium' (default), 'chrome'/'msedge', 'firefox', 'webkit'. NOTE: a schedule accepts only chromium/msedge/firefox/webkit.

headless.description: Headless. Defaults: cloud=true, local=false. (Immediate runs only.)

agentId.description: STEP 8 — for local: a credential_id from `local_agents` (this machine only; omit to auto-pick). For remote: REQUIRED — a credential_id from `remote_agents`. when:'immediate' → picked agent must be ONLINE; when:'schedule' → offline OK, agentId REQUIRED for both local and remote.

cloudRunnerId.description: STEP 8 (cloud) — a specific ONLINE runner id (from cloud_runners). For when:'schedule' omit to auto-pick a live VM at fire time.

strategy.description: STEP 3 (immediate runs) — SERIAL or PARALLEL across the suite's test cases: the same choice the UI's Execute-suite dialog shows as a PARALLEL/SERIAL radio, and it applies to LOCAL, REMOTE and CLOUD alike. ASK the user. RECOMMEND 'parallel' when the suite has several independent test cases (they run concurrently — much faster); recommend 'serial' when order or shared state matters. The wire defaults to SERIAL, which is why it must be asked rather than assumed.

maxConcurrent.description: Cloud parallel only — maps to globalConfiguration.MAXIMUM_CONTAINER_COUNT on the wire.

terminateOnFailure.description: Stop dispatching remaining test cases after the first failure. Maps to globalConfiguration.TERMINATE_ON_FAIL on the wire.

scheduledFor.description: STEP 6 — REQUIRED for when:'schedule'; ISO datetime of the first/only run (e.g. '2026-08-20T09:00:00Z').

scheduleType.description: SCHEDULE STEP — REQUIRED for when:'schedule'; ASK the user explicitly, never assume. The UI's Recurrence choices: 'once', 'every_5_minutes', 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'. Anything but 'once' also needs endDate. ('weekdays' = weekly Mon–Fri, MCP shortcut — don't offer it.)

endDate.description: SCHEDULE STEP — ISO end date; REQUIRED when scheduleType is anything but 'once'. ASK the user.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for a schedule (e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'). Default 'UTC'.

tools.name: run_status
tools.description:
Read the status of a run — state (queued/running/passed/failed/skipped/notExecuted/stopped/error), progress, per-test-case rollup for a SUITE run (capped at 100 shown, ONE ROW PER TEST CASE — not per iteration), and a link. Every state SQA reports is its own bucket in the per-state tally (skipped and notExecuted are real, distinct outcomes — never counted as passed or folded into queued). While the run is still queued/running, the tally is labelled provisional. Pass EITHER `runId` (from tc_run / suite_run) or `suiteId` (from suite_list) to read that suite's LATEST execution.

The suite rollup only says pass/fail/etc per test case, never WHY — to get one child's own step-level detail (which step failed, the error), call again with the SAME `runId`/`suiteId` plus `tcId` set to one of the ids shown in the rollup. Requires a live connection.

runId.description: The run id returned by tc_run or suite_run.

suiteId.description: A suite id (from suite_list) — resolves to the suite's latest execution.

tcId.description: Drill into ONE child test case's step-level results within a SUITE run — its id from the rollup shown by a prior run_status call (without `tcId`). Ignored / refused for a single-TC run.

tools.name: run_history
tools.description: Return the top-N most recent STANDALONE executions of a suite or test case (newest first), as a scoreboard — runId, state, timing, reportUrl, plus a per-test-case tally for SUITE runs (passed/failed/skipped of total). No step-level detail; use `run_status({ runId })` on any row to drill in. Pass EXACTLY one of `suiteId` or `tcId`. `limit` defaults to 5, capped at 20. Suite-child TC rows are excluded from a `tcId` query, so a test case that only runs inside suites returns empty. Requires a live connection.

suiteId.description: A suite id (from suite_list) — returns the suite's recent executions.

tcId.description: A test case id — returns the TC's recent STANDALONE executions.

limit.description: How many recent runs to return (default 5, max 20).

tools.name: run_stop
tools.description: Signal a running execution to stop, and poll briefly for the terminal state so the reply reflects reality (not a fire-and-forget). Pass EXACTLY one of: `runId` (from tc_run / suite_run), `suiteId` (stops the suite's LATEST execution), or `tcId` (stops the TC's LATEST standalone execution — suite-child rows are excluded). Requires a live connection.

suiteId.description: A suite id (from suite_list) — stops the suite's latest execution.

tcId.description: A test case id — stops the TC's latest STANDALONE execution.

tools.name: schedule_list
tools.description: List the scheduled runs in the connected project — each with WHAT it runs (test case / suite), its cadence, next run time, status (scheduled / running / paused / cancelled), where it runs + the pinned agent, and its browser. Use this to find a schedule to edit, pause/resume, cancel, or delete. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: schedule_update
tools.description: Change a schedule's time / recurrence / end date / timezone / browser / environment, or RE-PIN its agent. Pass `scheduleId` (from schedule_list) and ONLY the fields to change. To re-pin: mode:'local' + `agentId` (from local_agents), or mode:'cloud' + a runner's `cloudRunnerCredentialId` (the `credentialId` from cloud_runners). Requires a live connection.

scheduleType.description: New recurrence (same choices as the UI: once, every_5_minutes, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly). Anything but once needs an endDate.

endDate.description: New ISO end date (for recurring schedules).

browser.description: New browser (schedules accept chromium/msedge/firefox/webkit, not chrome).

mode.description: Re-pin target: pair with agentId (local) or cloudRunnerCredentialId (cloud).

agentId.description: Local re-pin: an agent credential_id from local_agents.

cloudRunnerCredentialId.description: Cloud re-pin: a runner's credentialId from cloud_runners.

tools.name: schedule_control
tools.description: Change a schedule's state: `pause` (stop it firing but keep it — reversible with `resume`), `resume` (re-enable a paused schedule), or `cancel` (stop its pending / live run). To remove a schedule entirely, use schedule_delete instead. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: schedule_delete
tools.description: Permanently DELETE a schedule (and tear down any run it currently owns). This cannot be undone — to only stop it temporarily use schedule_control (pause / cancel). CONFIRM with the user before deleting. Requires a live connection.

confirm.description: SimplifyQA: the first call only previews; pass true on the SECOND call, after the user explicitly said to delete.

tools.name: suite_manage
tools.description:
Change or remove an existing SimplifyQA suite. Pick ONE `action`:
- action:"update" — needs `suiteId` and at least one of `name`, `description`, `settings` (autoDefectLog, autoReExecCount, autoReExecTriggerOn, newBrowserSession, terminateOnFailure, minimumContainerCount, maximumContainerCount).
- action:"delete" — needs `suiteId`. TWO-STEP: call without `confirm` to PREVIEW (nothing is deleted), show it to the user, and call again with `confirm:true` ONLY after the user explicitly says to delete. A suite still used by a schedule, pipeline, execution plan or test plan is refused.
Add/remove member test cases with suite_add_testcases / suite_remove_testcases; create with suite_create.

action.description: What to do with the suite.

suiteId.description: Suite id or code (SU-12). Needed by every action.

confirm.description: action "delete": true on the SECOND call, only after the user explicitly said to delete.

tools.name: execution_plan
tools.description:
Manage SimplifyQA execution plans. Read plans with sqa_query (collection "executionPlans"). Pick ONE `action`:
- action:"create" — needs `name`, `plannedStartDate`, `plannedEndDate` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `environment` (name or key; see sqa_query collection "environments"). Optional: releaseId, sprintId, teamIds, planners, autoReExecCount, autoReExecTriggerOn, autoDefectLog, newBrowserSession, terminateOnFailure.
- action:"update" — needs `planId` and at least one field to change (same fields as create).
- action:"delete" — needs `planId`. TWO-STEP: call without `confirm` to PREVIEW (nothing is deleted; it states what is permanently lost), show it to the user, and call again with `confirm:true` ONLY after the user explicitly says to delete.
- action:"add_testcases" — needs `planId` and `tcIds` and/or `suiteIds` (a suite adds its test cases). Optional `assignTo` (user id or "me") and `assignDate` (YYYY-MM-DD); only assigned test cases can run. Duplicates are skipped.
- action:"remove_testcases" — needs `planId` and `tcIds`. TWO-STEP like delete: removing also DELETES those test cases' run history in SimplifyQA, which cannot be undone.
- action:"run" — needs `planId`; call ONLY when the user explicitly asked to run this plan. It runs NOW — SimplifyQA cannot schedule an execution plan (its Scheduler takes a test case or a suite). Runs LOCALLY on this machine's SimplifyQA agent (SimplifyQA runs plans locally; the agent must be running). Runs the assigned, non-blocked AUTOMATION test cases and says which were left out. Optional `agentId` (this machine's, see local_agents). Then track it with run_status({ runId }).
A plan in review or approval (REVIEW PENDING, APPROVE PENDING, REVIEWED, APPROVED) is read-only, as in SimplifyQA.

mode.description: run: only "local" is supported for plans.

agentId.description: run: this machine's agent id (optional; auto-picked, see local_agents).

when.description: run: only "immediate" — execution plans cannot be scheduled in SimplifyQA.

planId.description: Every action except create: plan id or code (PL-5).

tcIds.description: add_testcases / remove_testcases: test case ids or codes.

suiteIds.description: add_testcases: suites whose test cases to add.

name.description: create/update: plan name (unique in the project).

plannedEndDate.description: create/update: YYYY-MM-DD, on or after the start.

confirm.description: delete: true on the SECOND call, only after the user explicitly said to delete.

tools.name: test_plan
tools.description:
Manage SimplifyQA TEST PLANS (the Test Plan folders under Test Execution). Read them with sqa_query collection "testPlans". Actions:
- action:"create" — needs `name`; optional `parentId` (a test plan id) makes it a sub-folder.
- action:"rename" — needs `testPlanId` and `name`.
- action:"add" — needs `testPlanId` and `suiteIds` and/or `tcIds`; ones already in the test plan are skipped.
- action:"remove_suite" — needs `testPlanId` and `suiteId`.
- action:"remove_testcase" — NOT available: SimplifyQA's endpoint removes the wrong test case.
- action:"delete" — needs `testPlanId`. TWO-STEP: the first call only previews (it deletes every folder below it too); call again with `confirm:true` ONLY after the user explicitly says to delete.

testPlanId.description: Every action except create: test plan id or code.

parentId.description: create: parent test plan id (omit for a top-level one).

tcIds.description: add: test case ids or codes.

suiteId.description: remove_suite: the suite to take out.

tcId.description: remove_testcase: not available.

confirm.description: delete: true on the SECOND call, only after the user explicitly said to delete.

tools.name: pipeline
tools.description:
Manage SimplifyQA PIPELINES. Read them with sqa_query collection "pipelines". Actions:
- action:"create" — needs `name`, `pipelineType` (TC or SU), `parentId` (the test case or suite), `mode` (local / remote / cloud), `releaseId` and `sprintId` (SimplifyQA requires both — ASK if unknown); optional `agentId`, `environment`, `browser` (TC), `description`.
- action:"update" — needs `pipelineId`; any of `name`, `description`, `releaseId`, `sprintId`, `environment`, `agentId`, `mode`.
- action:"delete" — needs `pipelineId`. TWO-STEP: the first call only previews; call again with `confirm:true` ONLY after the user explicitly says to delete.
- action:"run" — needs `pipelineId`; call ONLY when the user explicitly asked to run it.
- action:"run_status" / "stop" — need `executionId` (from run).

pipelineId.description: update / delete / run: pipeline id or code.

executionId.description: run_status / stop: the execution id from run.

parentId.description: create: the test case or suite id / code.

releaseId.description: create / update: release id (required to create).

sprintId.description: create / update: sprint id (required to create).

environment.description: create / update: environment name or key (default general).

browser.description: create: browser for the WEB test cases — the test case, or every WEB test case in the suite (default chrome).

confirm.description: delete: true on the SECOND call, only after the user explicitly said to delete.

tools.name: tc_list_environments
tools.description: List every environment configured for the currently connected project (e.g. general, staging, production). Testdata is stored PER ENVIRONMENT — each env has its own iteration rows. ALWAYS call this before tc_get_testdata / tc_generate_testdata, show the user the options, and ASK which env they want to generate testdata for. Never assume. The value to pass onward as `environmentType` is the `key` field on each returned env.

tools.name: tc_get_testdata
tools.description:
Fetch the default iteration (template row) for TC `tcId` in a specific environment — the parameter list plus the CURRENT seed values. Testdata is per-env: seeds may differ across envs. `environmentType` is REQUIRED — this tool refuses when it is omitted, since silently guessing an env previously caused false "testdata not found" results. FIRST call tc_list_environments and ask the user which env they want. Then read the template here, and use the seeds + the test case's steps (from tc_get) to reason about realistic values before calling tc_generate_testdata.

When the TC has more than one version and `versionId` is omitted, this tool REFUSES and lists the available versions — ASK the user which one, then call again with `versionId`. Pass `versionId: ''` to accept the TC's currently-selected version. Single-version TCs are read directly.

FUNCTIONS: if a step in this TC calls a reusable FUNCTION, the `parameters` array (and the row list in this response's text) includes ONE extra row for it — a row whose "seed" is the function's NAME + VERSION, not its testdata (a called function's testdata is its own separate tc_get_testdata call, never guessed or fabricated here). It is a normal row in the SAME table as the TC's own parameters — do not pull it out into separate prose afterward. When one or more functions were called, this response ALSO ends with an explicit prompt listing each one and the exact tc_get_testdata args to fetch its testdata — ASK the user which (if any) they want BEFORE calling tc_get_testdata again for a function; do not fetch one unprompted, and do not skip the ask just because there is only one.

tools.name: tc_generate_testdata
tools.description:
Persist up to 20 testdata rows for TC `tcId` into a SPECIFIC environment. Testdata is stored per environment — rows saved here only affect the env you pass. WORKFLOW: (1) call tc_list_environments and ASK the user which env; (2) call tc_get_testdata with that env to read seeds; (3) call this tool with the SAME `environmentType`. `environmentType` is REQUIRED here — this tool refuses when it is omitted. Two ways to feed values:
  1) Model-generated — pass `rows: [{paramName: value}, ...]`. Call tc_get_testdata first for the parameter names + seeds, tc_get for step context, then produce rows that fit the flow.
  2) Formula-driven — pass `formulas: {paramName: {name, args?}}` (names from tc_list_formulas). Each formula is evaluated per row by the SimplifyQA desktop AGENT (the same engine the UI and the executor use, so every formula from tc_list_formulas works, including nested ones) and both the value and the source `=NAME(...)` expression are stamped. The agent must be running (QA_MCP_URL). For nested / custom formulas pass `expression` instead of `name`+`args`. Use `count` to say how many rows, or provide `rows` for constant columns; mixing is fine (formulas win over row values for the same param).
Rows are appended as new iterations; they do not become the default. Hard cap: 20 rows.

When the TC has more than one version and `versionId` is omitted, this tool REFUSES and lists the available versions — ASK the user which one, then call again with `versionId`. count.description: How many rows to generate when using formulas without explicit rows. Ignored if rows is set.

formulas.description: Per-column formula assignments applied to every row. Outer keys are param names from tc_get_testdata. Wins over rows[i] for the same key.

args.description: Named args. Keys MUST match Formula.parameters[].keyName exactly, no trailing colons or extra whitespace. Correct: {"country name": "United States"}. Wrong: {"country name:": "..."}.

expression.description: A complete formula, used as written — for nested or custom formulas, e.g. `=UPPER(FIRST_NAME("United States"))` or `=CONCATENATE(FIRST_NAME(),"@test.com")`. Use instead of name/args.

tools.name: tc_update_testdata
tools.description:
UPDATE the test data a run actually uses — the DEFAULT iteration (ITR-1) — instead of appending a new row. Use this for "change/set/fix the test data", "add a formula to the test data", or whenever a value or formula must apply to the NEXT run. (tc_generate_testdata APPENDS iterations; an appended row never becomes the default, so a formula saved there does not affect the run.)

Each cell takes a literal `value` or a `formula` ({ name, args? } from tc_list_formulas, or a full `expression` — nested formulas are supported). Formulas are evaluated by the SimplifyQA desktop agent; the evaluated value AND the canonical =NAME(...) expression are stored, and the executor re-evaluates at run time. Unknown/invented names and unevaluatable formulas are rejected BEFORE anything is written. Only the named cells change — every other column keeps its value — and the row is read back.

environmentType.description: Env `key` from tc_list_environments. REQUIRED — test data is per environment.

formula.description: Formula to store on that cell (takes precedence over `value`).

name.description: Raw formula name from tc_list_formulas (identifier only, no parens).

args.description: Formula arguments keyed by the formula's parameter keyName. Literal values only.

expression.description: Full expression — use for nested formulas, e.g. "=CONCATENATE(FULL_NAME(),CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER())".

cells.description: Cells to change. Only these are touched.

tools.name: tc_list_formulas
tools.description: Return the formulas the connected project can use for testdata generation — DEFAULT prefabs (FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME, COUNTRY_NAME, EMAIL_ID, PHONE_NUMBER, …) plus any CUSTOM formulas defined at customer or project scope. EVERY line starts with the NAME to pass as `name`; the parenthesised part after it is the human signature (it can differ — e.g. the name is EMAIL_ID while its signature reads EMAIL(...)), and `args:` lists the argument keys the formula accepts (matched case-insensitively). Feed a chosen `{name, args}` into `tc_generate_testdata.formulas` and that column is auto-filled fresh per row by the agent's formula engine. Use this when the user says "use a formula" / "generate an email" / "first name, phone, country…" / "list formulas".

tools.name: heal_plan
tools.description:
Replays a failed test case live, captures the DOM at the failing step, and returns a REVIEWABLE heal plan: objects (locators + properties), per-step actions, parameters, and the test data of the failing iteration only. This call never writes — apply it with `heal_apply({ planId })`.

Use it when a test failed for a reason the healer may fix (locator/object changed, wrong action, unresolved `${param}`, bad test-data value). It also reports a diagnosis when the failure is NOT healable (app bug, environment, bad business data), with the reason.

Rules baked in: the shared action catalog is never modified, shared parameters are never renamed (create + rebind instead), and only the iteration that failed may have test data patched.

tcId.description: The failing test case id (TC-123).

runId.description: Specific failed run. Omit to use the latest failed run.

domains.description: Limit which domains may change (default: all). e.g. ["parameter","testdata"] to skip locator churn.

url.description: Override start URL when the test case has no navigate step.

maxAttemptsPerStep.description: Replay retries at the failing step. Default 3.

testProposals.description: TEST ONLY (needs QA_HEAL_TEST_HOOK=1): plan these raw proposals instead of calling heal_propose. The full validation/apply pipeline runs exactly as in production; only the browser-driven proposal step is skipped.

testFamily.description: TEST ONLY: family to report alongside testProposals (default object_state).

tools.name: heal_apply
tools.description:
Applies a plan from `heal_plan` as ONE new test-case version: objects first, then step/action bindings, then the failing iteration's test data. The current version is never edited, so a running execution is not affected. `mode:"apply_and_verify"` also re-runs the test case and reports `verified` only when the healed step passes WITHOUT falling back to another locator.

Refuses a stale plan (the test case moved to a different version since planning) — re-run heal_plan then.

confirmSharedObject.description: Required when the plan changes an object also used by other test cases (blast radius non-empty).

tools.name: heal_status
tools.description: Returns the stored plan for a planId and, once applied, the apply report (version, verified, partial).

tools.name: tc_heal
tools.description:
One-shot alias for heal_plan + heal_apply. Default `mode:"suggest"` only diagnoses and proposes — it writes NOTHING. Pass `mode:"apply"` (new version) or `mode:"apply_and_verify"` (new version + re-run) to write.

Covers objects (locators/properties), actions (per step only — the catalog is never modified), parameters, and the test data of the failing iteration. Every response carries a classification and rationale, even when the failure is not healable (app bug, bad business data, environment).

tcId.description: The failing test case id.

runId.description: Specific failed run to heal against.

mode.description: Default 'suggest' (no writes). 'apply' persists a NEW version; 'apply_and_verify' also re-runs.

domains.description: Limit which domains may change (default: all).

url.description: Override start URL for the replay.

maxAttemptsPerStep.description: Replay retries at the failing step. Default 3.

confirmSharedObject.description: Required when applying a plan that changes an object used by other test cases.

testProposals.description: TEST ONLY (needs QA_HEAL_TEST_HOOK=1): plan these raw proposals instead of calling heal_propose. The full validation/apply pipeline runs exactly as in production; only the browser-driven proposal step is skipped.

testFamily.description: TEST ONLY: family to report alongside testProposals (default object_state).

tools.name: report_download
tools.description:
Generate and SAVE the PDF execution reports the SimplifyQA UI offers.
  • target "testcase" — report types: `detailed`, `summary` (pick one or both).
  • target "suite" — report types: `suite` (overall suite report), `detailed` (one detailed report per test case in the suite), `summary` (one summary report per test case). Pick one, several or all.
`ref` is the test case id/key (TC_123) or the suite NAME / id. If the user did NOT say which report type(s) they want, call WITHOUT `reportTypes` — the tool replies with the choices; ASK the user, then call again. If they named the type ("the summary pdf report"), pass it directly and do not ask. The report is for ONE execution: by default the most recent one, and the response states which execution was used and how many others exist — pass `runId` (execution id) to pick another. Files are saved under `outDir` (default ./qa-reports) and their paths returned. Protected parameters are masked by the report service. Requires a live connection; no agent needed.

target.description: Report for a test case or a suite.

ref.description: Test case id/key (TC_123), or suite name / id.

reportTypes.description: Which reports. Omit to get the choices and ASK the user. testcase: detailed | summary. suite: suite | detailed | summary.

runId.description: Execution id to report on. Omit to use the most recent execution.

outDir.description: Folder to save PDFs into. Default: ./qa-reports

tools.name: gap_analysis
tools.description:
Aggregate COVERAGE report — for a chosen scope, walks each story and reports which have no tests, which have ACs not covered by any linked test case, which have no acceptance criteria at all, and (for release / projectWide scopes) which TCs are unlinked to any story. READ-ONLY: writes nothing, but emits a "Next actions" hint block for the agent to chain into tc_draft_create / tc_draft_open+update+save / story_update after asking the user.

PICK EXACTLY ONE SCOPE — the tool errors if zero or more than one is provided:
  • `sprintId`    — recommended for sprint reviews
  • `releaseId`   — release readiness across all sprints in the release
  • `epicId`      — coverage on one epic
  • `featureId`   — coverage on one feature
  • `storyIds[]`  — hand-picked batch (or a single story: the same info story_sync_testcases returns, wrapped in the gap format)
  • `projectWide: true` — every story (expensive; prefer a narrower scope when the user's question is really about a sprint / release / area)

Reuses the same AC↔step matching as `story_sync_testcases` (Jaccard, sensitivity strict / normal / loose). Automation test cases COUNT toward `tcCount` but do NOT run drift (their steps are recorded, not AC-derived — computeDrift would false-flag every AC as uncovered). Orphan-TC detection runs only for `releaseId` / `projectWide` scopes.

When the user's question is about a single story, prefer `story_sync_testcases` if they want the drift ops to apply; use this tool if they want a coverage verdict / report.

epicId.description: Epic numeric id or business key (EP_123).

featureId.description: Feature numeric id or business key (FT_123).

projectWide.description: Set true to scan every story in the project (bounded by scanLimit). Prefer a narrower scope when possible — projectWide fans out into many adapter calls.

sensitivity.description: AC↔step match strictness (same as story_sync_testcases). Default `normal`.

scanLimit.description: Cap on the initial listStories fetch (and, for release/projectWide, the orphan-TC scan). Default 500. Raise for a genuinely huge project.

tools.name: impact_analysis
tools.description:
BLAST-RADIUS report from ONE anchor — walks the graph both ways to answer "if this is broken / unfinished, what does it affect?" READ-ONLY.

PICK EXACTLY ONE ANCHOR:
  • `defectId`   (DF_77) — walks defect → TC(s) → story → sprint → release, then sibling stories in the sprint.
  • `testCaseId` (TC_204) — walks TC → open defects on it → story → sprint → release.
  • `storyId`    (US_103) — walks story → its TCs / defects / sprint / release / sibling stories.
  • `sprintId`   — rolls up every story in the sprint: uncovered ACs, open critical / major defects, stories with no tests.
  • `releaseId`  — per-sprint table with a rolled-up release verdict.

VERDICT (traffic light, deliberately simple):
  · `AT_RISK`         — any open critical defect, OR more than 30% of ACs uncovered.
  · `NEEDS_ATTENTION` — any open major defect, OR a story in scope has zero tests.
  · `READY`           — otherwise.

Reuses `gap_analysis`'s per-story analyser to count uncovered ACs, so the AC↔step match rules (Jaccard, sensitivity) are consistent between the two tools. Writes nothing — any triage the user chooses (reassign, descope, add TC) goes through the existing write tools after they confirm.

sensitivity.description: AC↔step match strictness passed through to gap analysis. Default `normal`.

scanLimit.description: Cap on the initial listStories fetch for sprint/release rollups. Default 500.

instructions:
You are driving the Common QA MCP (common-qa-mcp), which fronts a QA product (Walnut or SimplifyQA).

GROUND RULES (all providers, always):
- FIRST turn: call `qa_connection_status` to see what is connected and which project is active.
  If not connected, call `qa_connect({ url, token, projectId })`.
- Project is NEVER assumed. If none is active, list the user's projects (SimplifyQA: `sqa_query({ op:"search", collection:"projects", where:[{ field:"member", value:true }] })`; Walnut: `list_projects`) and ASK the user which one, then `qa_switch_project`.
- NEVER save without an EXPLICIT user instruction ("save it" / "persist it"). A finished recording is a DRAFT - stop and show it. "Looks good" is approval of content, NOT permission to save. ONE EXCEPTION: an API recording auto-saves ONCE after its LAST api_send_request (see API below), so the recorded test case is searchable without clicking Send and Save.
- NEVER call an MCP endpoint directly with curl / Invoke-RestMethod / raw JSON-RPC. NEVER shell out to work around a failing tool. If a tool errors or is missing, REPORT the error and STOP — do not synthesize a workaround.
- Follow each tool's own description — many tools RETURN a numbered guide in their response (notably `tc_record_append`). Do exactly what the returned guide says.
- If the user asks for something this MCP does not expose (e.g. activity / audit / login logs), say plainly that it is not available here and stop. NEVER answer with a look-alike collection (scheduleHistory is scheduler runs, not an activity log).
- When a result carries a `visibility` note (SimplifyQA users / projects), the list is only what THIS user can see. Say so in the answer ("341 users who share a project with you"), never "all users" / "every project".
RECORDING: provider is not yet resolved. Call `qa_connection_status` first — the response names the product, and the per-tool descriptions from `tools/list` will guide the flow (SimplifyQA uses granular verbs orchestrated via `tc_record_append`; Walnut uses the bundled `web` sub-agent).
